setting.world: Real Edwardian London combined with the magical Neverland island
setting.description: A proper London townhouse nursery at No.14 with night-lights, beds, and a kennel, connected by flight to a compact magical tropical island with lagoon, Marooners' Rock, forests, underground home with hollow-tree entrances, redskin camp, and pirate brig Jolly Roger offshore.

characters.name: Peter Pan
characters.physical_description: A lovely small boy just Wendy's size with all his first teeth like little pearls, slender and light build. Typically clad only in skeleton leaves and the juices that ooze out of trees.

characters.name: Wendy Darling
characters.physical_description: A little girl of two growing to pre-teen years with a neat tidy appearance. Usually in a nightgown and later a house dress, with a chain around her neck and her hair kept tidy.

characters.name: John Darling
characters.physical_description: A school-aged boy of medium build, slightly practical looking. Usually in night clothes and later a Sunday hat, and pirate clothes cut off at the knee.

characters.name: Michael Darling
characters.physical_description: A very small young boy, the littlest of the three, sharp-featured. Usually in a pinafore then shirts and night clothes, later carried in a basket and in pirate garb.

characters.name: George Darling
characters.physical_description: A thin city gentleman with a moustache and balding head, concerned about Stocks and shares. Typically in office suit, new braided trousers, tie he cannot tie, and evening dress.

characters.name: Mrs. Darling
characters.physical_description: A lovely lady with a romantic look and a sweet mocking mouth with a kiss in the right-hand corner. Usually in a white evening gown with a necklace and Wendy's bracelet on her arm.

characters.name: Nana
characters.physical_description: A large prim black Newfoundland dog with shaggy fur and soulful wet eyes. Acts as nurse, often carrying an umbrella in her mouth and wearing no clothing.

characters.name: Liza
characters.physical_description: A tiny midget-like maidservant with a small slight figure. Wears a long skirt and a maid's cap, often with flour or a raisin on her cheek from cooking.

characters.name: Tinker Bell
characters.physical_description: A tiny fairy girl no longer than a hand, slightly inclined to embonpoint with a glowing light. Exquisitely gowned in a skeleton leaf cut low and square.

characters.name: Tootles
characters.physical_description: A round chubby boy, larger than Peter, with a gentle melancholy countenance. Wears the skin of a bear slain by himself, very round and furry.

characters.name: Nibs
characters.physical_description: A lean gay and debonair boy, larger in breadth than Peter. Wears a round furry bear skin.

characters.name: Slightly
characters.physical_description: A rather stout conceited boy with an uptilted nose, the most swollen of the boys from drinking water. Wears a furry bear skin.

characters.name: Curly
characters.physical_description: A pickle-faced boy with curly hair, round and sturdy in build. Wears a furry bear skin.

characters.name: The Twins
characters.physical_description: Two identical vague small boys, round and furry and indistinguishable from each other. Both wear bear skins and keep close together.

characters.name: James Hook
characters.physical_description: A tall cadaverous blackavized man with long black curls like black candles, blue forget-me-not eyes, and handsome countenance. Dressed in Charles II style with lace collar and doublet, smoking two cigars, with an iron hook instead of his right hand.

characters.name: Smee
characters.physical_description: An oddly genial stocky Irish bo'sun with spectacles and a kind round face. Dressed as a pirate in rough seaman's clothes, carrying a cutlass.

characters.name: Starkey
characters.physical_description: A tall dainty former school usher turned pirate, neat in manner. Dressed in pirate clothes with a cutlass, with a tarpaulin hat.

characters.name: Cecco
characters.physical_description: A handsome tall Italian pirate with great bare arms and pieces of eight in his ears as ornaments. Dressed in rough pirate garb.

characters.name: Bill Jukes
characters.physical_description: A burly heavily tattooed pirate covered in tattoos on every inch. Dressed in rough pirate seaman's clothing.

characters.name: Tiger Lily
characters.physical_description: A beautiful young Piccaninny princess with copper-brown skin, dark hair, and erect proud carriage. Bare except for paint, beads, and a blanket, carrying tomahawk and knife.

characters.name: Great Big Little Panther
characters.physical_description: A stocky muscular redskin brave with naked gleaming painted body hung with scalps. Moves on all fours in the van, wearing tribal paint and loincloth.

characters.name: Jane
characters.physical_description: A small girl with an odd inquiring look, much like Wendy as a child. Usually in a nightdress in bed, with short child hair.

characters.name: Margaret
characters.physical_description: A little girl daughter of Jane, small and childlike. Usually seen in night clothes as a young child.

chapters.title: PETER BREAKS THROUGH
chapters.summary: Chapter 1 introduces the happy Darling family at No.14 and their dog-nurse Nana, where Wendy learns she must grow up. Mrs. Darling discovers the name Peter Pan scrawled through her children's minds and hears Wendy's story of night visits and skeleton leaves by the three-storey window. On Nana's night off, Mrs. Darling falls asleep sewing by the fire and wakes as the window blows open and Peter Pan breaks through from the Neverland with his fairy light.
chapters.cover_description: Night nursery interior with three small beds and night-lights, tall window blown open to night sky, a small boy clad in skeleton leaves dropping to the floor baring pearl-like first teeth, accompanied by a darting fist-sized fairy light, as a lady in a white evening gown wakes by the fireside with sewing in her lap.

chapters.title: THE SHADOW
chapters.summary: Mrs. Darling captures Peter's detached shadow after Nana chases him from the nursery window and hides it in a drawer. A week later on a fatal Friday, Mr. Darling's pride over medicine and his tie leads him to drug Nana's milk and chain her in the yard. With the parents gone to dinner at No. 27 and the night-lights lit, the stars call for Peter to return.
chapters.cover_description: Nana the huge black Newfoundland springs at a small boy escaping through the nursery window, snapping off his detached shadow as Mrs. Darling in her white evening gown screams in the starry black night.

chapters.title: COME AWAY, COME AWAY!
chapters.summary: Peter Pan slips into the Darling nursery with Tinker Bell to recover his shadow, which Wendy sews back on. He charms Wendy with tales of Neverland, fairies, and the Lost Boys, trading thimble-kisses and provoking Tink's jealousy. After evading Nana and Liza, Peter teaches Wendy, John and Michael to fly with fairy dust and lures them out the window just before Mr. and Mrs. Darling return too late.
chapters.cover_description: Moonlit Victorian nursery at night with window blown open by starlight, Peter Pan in skeleton leaves blowing glittering fairy dust as Wendy, John and Michael in nightclothes soar joyfully bobbing against the ceiling, tiny glowing Tinker Bell darting nearby.

chapters.title: THE FLIGHT
chapters.summary: Peter leads Wendy, John and Michael on a long, perilous flight to the Neverland, feeding them from birds and catching them as they fall asleep, while Wendy fears they cannot stop or return without him and that forgetful Peter will forget them. As the familiar make-believe island turns real and threatening at nightfall, Peter names Captain Jas. Hook and makes John promise to leave Hook to him, then hides Tink's betraying light in John's hat. The pirates fire Long Tom, scattering the children, lea
chapters.cover_description: Wendy, John, Michael and Peter Pan flying high in night sky toward the distant Neverland island lit by a million golden arrows of sunlight, with tiny glowing Tinker Bell circling them in a halo of fairy light above dark seas and lagoon below.

chapters.title: THE ISLAND COME TRUE
chapters.summary: With Peter returning, the Neverland's lost boys, pirates, redskins, beasts and crocodile circle the island in pursuit of each other. The boys hide in their underground home while Hook discovers their chimney, plots to poison them with a green-sugar cake, and flees the ticking crocodile that ate his severed arm. After the boys drive off wolves by looking through their legs, jealous Tinker Bell tricks Tootles into shooting down Wendy as she flies overhead.
chapters.cover_description: A weary girl in a nightgown falling from the night sky over Neverland with an arrow in her breast, while a tiny glowing fairy darts jealously around her and round furry bearskin boys below aim bows.

chapters.title: THE LITTLE HOUSE
chapters.summary: After Tootles shoots down Wendy, the lost boys despair until they discover Peter's kiss-button on her chain saved her life, and Peter banishes Tinker Bell for a week for her treachery. To honor without touching her, the boys build a make-believe little house around Wendy, and she awakens to accept them as her children, tucking them in while Peter stands guard outside.
chapters.cover_description: A tiny cozy little house built around a sleeping girl in a moonlit Neverland wood, with red sap-sticky walls, mossy green roof, roses at the windows, smoke rising from a hat chimney, lamplight glowing through leaf blinds while a boy with a drawn sword stands guard outside.

chapters.title: THE HOME UNDER THE GROUND
chapters.summary: Peter fits Wendy, John and Michael for hollow trees to enter the cozy underground home with its mushroom stools, Never-tree table, sardine bed, and Tink's exquisite boudoir. Wendy settles into endless motherly cooking and sewing while realizing John and Michael are forgetting their London parents and testing them with school exams. Bored with daily fights, Peter invents a game of having no adventures, before the narrator tosses among many true and half-true island adventures and chooses the lago
chapters.cover_description: The cozy underground home lit warmly, with stout mushroom stools around a living Never-tree table, the sardine bed tilted against the earthen wall, Wendy sewing among the boys, and Tinker Bell's tiny curtained bird-cage boudoir glowing in the wall.

chapters.title: THE MERMAIDS’ LAGOON
chapters.summary: On a sunny day at Mermaids' Lagoon the children rest on Marooners' Rock until pirates arrive to maroon Tiger Lily to drown. Peter tricks the pirates by imitating Hook's voice to free her, then reveals himself, leading to a fight where Hook unfairly bites him and flees the crocodile. Stranded with Wendy on the rising tide and unable to fly or swim, Peter sends her to safety on Michael's kite and faces death alone as an awfully big adventure.
chapters.cover_description: Peter Pan standing erect alone on the tiny shrinking Marooners' Rock at night as moonlit water rises around him, pale rays tiptoeing across the lagoon while mermaids call to the moon.

chapters.title: THE NEVER BIRD
chapters.summary: Stranded alone on the rock as the tide rises, Peter is rescued by the Never bird, who offers him her floating nest despite having eggs in it. After a comic failure to understand each other, Peter floats the eggs safely in Starkey's watertight hat and sails ashore in the nest. He reaches the home under the ground to great rejoicing, where Wendy sternly sends the late, boastful boys to bed.
chapters.cover_description: Peter Pan sailing away from a half-submerged rock in a lagoon in a giant bird's nest boat with his shirt raised as a sail on a stave mast, while the Never bird drifts the opposite way sitting on her two white eggs floating in Starkey's broad-brimmed tarpaulin hat.

chapters.title: THE HAPPY HOME
chapters.summary: After saving Tiger Lily, Peter is worshipped as the Great White Father by the redskins who guard the underground home. On the Night of Nights the Darlings and lost boys share a rowdy make-believe tea and a tender fireside evening with Wendy as mother, but Peter admits his fatherhood is only make-believe, sparking Wendy's jealousy. Unaware of the coming pirate attack, the children enjoy one last glad hour of dancing and stories before bed.
chapters.cover_description: The lost boys and Darlings in nightgowns dancing and pillow-fighting around the warm fire in the cozy underground home, with Wendy sewing by the fireside and Peter watching — their last glad hour together.

chapters.title: WENDY’S STORY
chapters.summary: Wendy tells the lost boys her story of the Darlings and a mother's always-open window, promising a happy return home. Peter shatters the tale by revealing his own mother barred her window and forgot him, frightening Wendy into deciding to leave for London at once with John, Michael, and the lost boys. Peter refuses to come, insisting on remaining a little boy forever, just as pirates attack the redskins above while the children prepare to depart.
chapters.cover_description: Wendy telling her bedtime story to seven boys crowded in a bed in the lamplit underground home while Peter leans apart playing his pipes, as Tinker Bell glows nearby before the pirate attack erupts above.

chapters.title: THE CHILDREN ARE CARRIED OFF
chapters.summary: Hook breaks the laws of savage warfare by ambushing the Piccaninnies waiting to attack at dawn, massacring Tiger Lily's warriors while a remnant escapes. Exultant but fixated on Peter Pan, whose cockiness drives his hatred, Hook plots to reach the boys below. He has Smee beat the captured tom-tom to fake an Indian victory, luring the cheering children up the trees into ambush.
chapters.cover_description: Pirate captain Hook and his crew falling treacherously upon Tiger Lily and her Piccaninny warriors in the grey pre-dawn forest above the children's underground home, cutlasses raised in a surprise massacre.

chapters.title: DO YOU BELIEVE IN FAIRIES?
chapters.summary: Hook captures Wendy and the boys and discovers Slightly's widened tree, giving him secret access to Peter's underground home. While Peter sleeps Hook poisons his medicine, and Tinker Bell drinks it to save him, falling deathly faint. Peter's plea for dreaming children to believe in fairies and clap saves Tink, and Peter sets out on foot on a cloudy moonlit night vowing 'Hook or me' to rescue Wendy.
chapters.cover_description: A small boy in skeleton leaves kneeling beside a tiny glowing fairy girl fading on her little bed in a dark underground room, pleading outward with flung arms while holding a poisoned cup, moonless night gloom around them.

chapters.title: THE PIRATE SHIP
chapters.summary: Aboard the Jolly Roger at night Hook broods alone over good form while his pirates hold the captured boys chained below. Hook offers two boys a place as cabin boys, but John, Michael and the others refuse to renounce King and mothers and are condemned to walk the plank, with Wendy tied to the mast to watch. Just as Hook gloats, the tick of the crocodile freezes him in terror, only for the boys to discover it is Peter come to rescue them.
chapters.cover_description: The pirate brig Jolly Roger looming low and dark on moonless night water off Kidd's Creek, Captain Hook in lace doublet and iron hook cowering on deck while a small boy Peter Pan climbs the ship's side ticking like the crocodile, with chained Lost Boys and Wendy tied to the mast watching.

chapters.title: “HOOK OR ME THIS TIME”
chapters.summary: Peter imitates the tick of the run-down crocodile-clock to swim to and board Hook's brig, then ambushes Hook's pirates one by one from the cabin while the boys count the kills. Revealing himself as Peter Pan the avenger, he leads the boys to slay the crew and duels Hook in single combat until Hook, foiled in blowing up the ship, leaps overboard to the waiting crocodile to avoid showing bad form. Afterwards Wendy takes charge and puts the victors to bed while Peter sleeps restlessly by Long Tom.
chapters.cover_description: Peter Pan with dagger poised dueling Captain Hook with hook and sword on the moonlit deck of the pirate brig, the ticking crocodile waiting in the dark water below the bulwark.

chapters.title: THE RETURN HOME
chapters.summary: Peter captains the pirate ship home toward the mainland while Mr. Darling atones by living in Nana's kennel until the children return. Slipping first into the nursery, Peter plots to bar the window to keep Wendy, but Mrs. Darling's tears make him unbar it and fly away. Wendy, John and Michael return to an emotional reunion while Peter watches forever excluded from that joy.
chapters.cover_description: A lonely small boy in skeleton leaves staring in through an open nursery window at night at a joyful family embrace around a fireplace, with a dog kennel and small beds visible inside the warm lamplit nursery.

chapters.title: WHEN WENDY GREW UP
chapters.summary: The Lost Boys are adopted by the Darlings while Peter refuses to grow up and secures Wendy for a week each spring to do his cleaning. As years pass the boys lose the power to fly and Wendy grows into a wife and mother, forgetting Peter until he returns unchanged one spring night and, unable to take grown Wendy, flies away with her daughter Jane to begin the endless cycle of mothers.
chapters.cover_description: Night nursery window blown open to a starry spring sky, small boy Peter Pan with all his first teeth crowing on a bed-post while little Jane in her nightdress flies around the room, grown-up Wendy in white darning by the fire watching them recede as small as stars.
